metadata.title: pH 7.3 major-microspecies benchmark for ChEBI (Rhea mapping, open RDKit rules)
metadata.description:
A benchmark for predicting the major protonation state of ChEBI compounds at pH 7.3. It pairs 113,385 ChEBI entities with Rhea's chebi_pH7_3_mapping.tsv (8,402 of which map to a different protonation form) and adds predictions from open, RDKit-only rules (chemrof.converter.protonation).

Version 2026-10-14: the default predictions now come from clean-room rules derived only from measured pKa values (raw ChEMBL25/DataWarrior extracts, CC BY 4.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.7884512) and textbook group pKas, never from Rhea's mapping, whose changed rows are computed (reportedly by ChemAxon). Predictions from the earlier Rhea-fitted rules are included for comparison. Against measured pKa on 2,152 held-out IUPAC molecules the clean-room rules score 89.5% (Rhea-fitted 89.4%); on the 217 that Rhea covers, 95.9% vs 94.5% for ChemAxon. Agreement with Rhea's changed rows is 90.2% (Rhea-fitted 91.6%).

Files: benchmark.parquet (mapping rows with structures, split and predictions from three rule sets); disagreements.parquet; chebi_structures.parquet (ChEBI SMILES used, with structures whose ChEBI SMILES fail to parse rebuilt from molfiles); chebi_unparseable_smiles.parquet (13,171 ChEBI SMILES that RDKit cannot parse, mostly a missing H on aromatic N-H); the exact Rhea file used; a data card and SHA256 checksums.

Derived from ChEBI and Rhea (both CC BY 4.0); please cite them when using this dataset.
metadata.notes: Version 2026-10-14 built with chemkg/chemrof chebi-scratch/ph73/make_bundle.py; see DATACARD.md for the commit. The sealed split has already been scored, so it is not a blind test set.
